newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich details share auction timetable.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich details share auction timetable.

text.p: Britain's Woolwich Building Society said on Thursday it would announce on Friday how many of its members have elected to sell their shares through an auction process when it floats on the London stock exchange next week.

A Woolwich spokeswoman told Reuters the announcement would be made via the stock exchange on Friday and the auctions to institutional shareholders would be held after the close of trading on July 7,8,9 and 10 with members receiving the average price.
The value of their shares would be known on July 11, she added. The flotation itself takes place on Monday July 7.
City Index, which last month opened a spread betting book on the Woolwich closing price on the day of its flotation, quoted the price at 316 pence bid, 324 pence offered.
This was lower than the bookmaker's opening quote of 327 pence bid, 337 pence offered.

Around 2.5 million members will receive a minimum of 250 free shares from among the 1.6 billion pounds being listed when Woolwich ditches its mutuality -- where it was owned by its savers and borrowers -- in favour of becoming a bank.
City Index's mid-price would give the Woolwich a market capitalisation of around 5.1 billion stg, which would see it qualify for the FTSE-100 share index.
